claim: Layer-stratified rerun of the H1/H2/H3 onset-hierarchy pipeline (Andre's ask, relayed via Hamm: 'How about also looking into the layer where these cells are located'), joining outputs/layers/unit_layers.csv (vFLIP2 putative sup/mid/deep) onto the same unit-class table fit_class_onset_latency.py already uses.
method: scripts/fit_class_onset_latency_by_layer.py (new file, imports and reuses fit_class_onset_latency.py's functions rather than duplicating them). Run on the full 22-session corpus, on top of the boundary-pinning fix in artifacts/.lab/onset-hierarchy-h1h2h3-fixed-20260815.json.

coverage.unit_level_layer_coverage: 2853/9056 units (31.5%) carry a real sup/mid/deep label
coverage.caveat: Per PROJECT_STATE.md section 5, coverage is not balanced across animal or area (Kruskal-Wallis H=12.80, P=0.0017 on channel-level coverage) -- a laminar comparison pooled across areas/animals would carry that imbalance inside it, not just cortex.

cells.note: wide CI spans down to ~0 -- underpowered, not a clean estimate

consistent with the omnibus-deep MT cell above (same units dominate both, expected)

STILL BOUNDARY-PINNED despite the fix -- inspected cell_fits_by_layer.csv directly: 2 of 3 gate-passing sessions have t0 at machine-epsilon, the 3rd at t0=1.04ms (right at the pin threshold). The widened baseline window (-400,-150ms) was not far enough back for this specific area x layer cell. DO NOT read 0.35ms as a finding.

interpretation: Not enough data for a layer-hierarchy conclusion. The one area with all three layers represented (PFC) shows a suggestive sup(105)->mid(116)->deep(122) ordering -- but n=3-4 sessions per layer, CIs overlapping heavily, and PFC alone cannot support a laminar claim per the same-area-same-animal caveat above. No hierarchy_test (rank-correlation) was run on this output -- with only 1-3 areas represented per layer, there are nowhere near the 4-area minimum that function itself requires, so it would not produce a meaningful number.
recommendation: Do not report any number from this run as a finding. The honest conclusion is a power ceiling: with current session count and ~31% unit-level layer coverage, layer-stratified onset comparison is not yet possible for any class. Revisit once either (a) more sessions are added, or (b) vFLIP2 coverage improves. This is the same ceiling PROJECT_STATE.md section 6 already documents for the laminar sign question generally -- this result is additional confirmation, not a new problem.
